review_scope: Full 68-unit Chinese–English alignment read including table, title/deck, withdrawal of the Sunzi hierarchy attribution, all stated limits and empirical disclaimers. Four local corrections; otherwise existing full English retained.

changes.before: Attack by Fire, closing passage — the place in the Sunzi that most resembles a self-limitation: no ruler should put troops into the field merely to gratify his own spleen; no general should fight a battle simply out of pique. If it is to your advantage, make a forward move; if not, stay where you are. Anger may in time change to gladness; vexation may be succeeded by content. But a kingdom that has once been destroyed can never come again into being; nor can the dead ever be brought back to life. Hence the enlightened ruler is heedful, and the good general full of caution. Calculations opens in the same direction: the art of war is of vital importance to the state, a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin.
changes.after: Attack by Fire, closing passage — the place in the Sunzi that most resembles a self-limitation: no ruler should put troops into the field merely to gratify his own spleen; no general should fight a battle simply out of pique. If it is to your advantage, make a forward move; if not, stay where you are. Anger may in time change to gladness; vexation may be succeeded by content. But a kingdom that has once been destroyed can never come again into being; nor can the dead ever be brought back to life. Hence the enlightened ruler is heedful, and the good general full of caution. Calculations opens in the same direction: the art of war is of vital importance to the state, a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin; it must be examined with the utmost care.
changes.reason: Restore 不可不察也, the express requirement of examination in the opening quotation.

changes.before: Theorem One's two conditions are not of that class: has the carrier of cultivation been lost; can cultivation in its mild forms no longer continue. These two ask: before war begins, what state is that relation in — are the non-war roads still open. And the domain must be stated, because this is very easily read as a judgement about the whole Sunzi. It is not. The book contains a great deal asking after other things — form, force and vacuity ask after the balance of strength; Employment of Spies asks after channels of information; and the four rungs from the highest form of generalship is to baulk the enemy's plans downward ask after the available sequence of means, which stands closer to the state of a relation than to the properties of a war. This proposition claims only what each of the three passages asks after.

changes.reason: Restore both halves of 虚实 rather than translate only emptiness.

changes.before: Sunzi's reason is the usability that comes with wholeness. A country taken whole is still usable — its people, its produce, its walls, its fields are all there; shattered, there is less of it. Waging War has the direct counterpart: the enemy's spoils are used to augment one's own strength. A qualification must be entered, because this is easily read too narrowly: calling it a pure cost argument would be too strong — what quan preserves is not only convertible resources but structures of governance, populations, and the subsequent capacity to control the place. Nor is not-fighting a zero-cost limit: breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting requires investment in attacking-the-plan and breaking-alliances, requires the accumulation of positional advantage, requires the other side to accept. What this volume uses is the weaker step: Sunzi's preference for quan rests on there being a difference in usability between whole and shattered, and that difference can vary.
changes.after: Sunzi's reason is the usability that comes with wholeness. A qualification must be entered, because this is easily read too narrowly: calling it a pure cost argument would be too strong — what quan preserves is not only convertible resources but structures of governance, populations, and the subsequent capacity to control the place. Nor is not-fighting a zero-cost limit: breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting requires investment in attacking-the-plan and breaking-alliances, requires the accumulation of positional advantage, requires the other side to accept. What this volume uses is the weaker step: Sunzi's preference for quan rests on there being a difference in usability between whole and shattered, and that difference can vary.
changes.reason: Do not narrow 胜敌而益强 to the use of spoils alone.

changes.before: And a downstream consequence: part of a load-bearing member's support has moved. With Sunzi ranked mou above gui withdrawn, the question arises whether SAE's four-rung hierarchy of means has support independent of Sunzi — its legitimacy previously depended in part on the attribution that Sunzi had already drawn a comparable distinction, and that attribution is now withdrawn. Two volumes of this series rest on it: volume three, whose recoil mechanism and first test question issue from §12; and volume seven, whose matching of Gandhi's satyagraha rests on one rung of the hierarchy. Each carries a registration; and the re-argument of the hierarchy itself belongs to §12 of the treatise, not to this series. This series can point out the gap; it cannot fill it.
